source.title: Vision CNNs trained to estimate spatial latents learned similar ventral-stream-aligned representations
source.authors: Yu-Di Xie; Wei-Chen Huang; Esther Alter; Jeremy Schwartz; Joshua B. Tenenbaum; J. DiCarlo

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some numerical results are presented only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures representation similarity and finds it is high but incomplete, varies by layer, and is partly shaped by variation in non-target latents in the training data.
record.gate_note: Rows cover CKA representation-similarity results and comparisons of non-target-latent decoding under full versus reduced training-data variability. Neural alignment with the brain, behavioral alignment, target-task performance, and dataset-size trends are not rows because they do not directly measure the representation convergence named in the claim. The discussion of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis is background, not a result from that work.
record.test_reason: The paper measures linear CKA between ResNet-18s trained on different spatial and category targets with shared data, and seed-to-seed CKA within each target. It then causally varies non-target latent variability in the shared training data and measures how this changes cross-model and cross-seed CKA. This bears on V7 (incomplete convergence, driven by shared data) and on V3 (seed convergence). The main topic, ventral-stream neural alignment, is not representation convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors' primary conclusion concerns the ventral stream: spatial-latent-trained CNNs reach neural alignment comparable to category-trained ones, so the ventral stream need not be optimized only for categorization. Secondary conclusions: the models' representations are similar but not identical, especially in early and middle layers. Non-target latent variability in the shared data partly explains this convergence, alongside other factors such as rendering and stimulus statistics.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses supervised ResNet-18 models trained on synthetic images and linear CKA, plus controlled changes to non-target latent variability. It does not reproduce the original cross-modal scale comparison or the original convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: Representation similarity varies by layer; the study reports greater similarity in early and middle layers and divergence in late layers. Training-data variability also changes CKA similarity and non-target decoding outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18s trained on different targets (distance, translation, rotation, category) with the same data have high linear CKA in early-middle layers, often within seed-to-seed variation, and diverge at layer4.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks with the same architecture and data but different supervised objectives converge in early and middle layers and diverge in late layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Greater variability in a non-target latent in the training data improves linear decodability of that latent in intermediate layers. Category-trained models instead become more translation-invariant in avgpool/fc.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data variability in untargeted factors causes models to encode those factors, a proposed mechanism for cross-objective convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Full non-target variability raises Brain-Score neural alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-target data variability increases model-brain alignment.

record.problems: The representation comparisons use one architecture family, synthetic TDW images, and linear CKA on 2000 held-out images. Several relevant values are only shown in figures. The authors note that representation differences may be subtler than the measures detect and that rendering and stimulus statistics may also shape similarity.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were omitted for the 60-row limit. Figure E.3 neural-alignment outcomes are recorded separately but are not used for convergence verdicts because they do not directly measure representation similarity.

untested.parts: No sweep of size or capability. A single architecture family is trained on one synthetic dataset. Only training objectives vary.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
No unit-level or subspace-level matching; only aggregate linear CKA across seeds.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
Linear CKA and the 2000 TDW test images are fixed throughout. No alternative metrics, kernel settings or out-of-distribution evaluation inputs.
No test of plateauing with scale. No contrast between the shared-data explanation and a 'common model of reality'. No comparison across broadly different datasets.

missing.what: CKA of TDW-trained models (all targets) and untrained models against ImageNet-1K-trained ResNet-18s across layers. This is a cross-training-data comparison; values are shown only in the figure.
CKA between category-trained models and each spatial-target model by layer, including the intra-category seed reference.
MDS of the model similarity matrix, showing spatial-target models mixed until layer4.0.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. All convergence evidence is linear CKA, given only in figures. The training-data manipulation concerns the causes of convergence (V7), not measurement dependence (V6), so the reader's V6 links were removed. The authors frame their result as compatible with Huh et al., saying models may be 'learning the world'. They therefore do not argue against the Platonic view, only that shared data variability is a partial driver.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model size or capability for representation similarity; the compared models use the same architecture.
No paired vision-language models or image-caption representations.
The study compares representations across random initializations and objectives, but does not identify recurring individual units, interpretable features, or shared subspaces directly.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
The study varies training-data latent variability while keeping the CKA method fixed. It does not compare similarity metrics or test out-of-distribution inputs for CKA.

The study manipulates non-target-latent variability in synthetic training data, but does not compare broadly different datasets, architectures, or training objectives to isolate shared-data or shared-objective effects.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18s on TDW-117, layer3/layer4, with full vs reduced non-target (category or translation) variability
relationships.reason: Full non-target variability made models more similar to models trained on that latent (R9, R10) and seeds more similar in layer4 (R11, R12). Cross-target similarity stays incomplete in late layers (R4).
relationships.display_finding: Full non-target variability increased similarity to models trained on that latent and increased layer4 similarity across seeds, while late-layer similarity across targets remained incomplete.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: ResNet-18s on TDW-117, layer3/layer4, with full vs reduced non-target (category or translation) variability
source_check.reason: R4 establishes late-layer divergence; R9–R12 establish a contribution from training-data variability in most comparisons. Rotation exceptions are separately qualified by l1. These results support the tested incompleteness and data-contribution aspects of V7.

relationships.reason: The data-variability effect on CKA fails or is unclear for rotation-trained models, which have large SD (R9 layer4, R10, R11, R12). Authors call non-target variability only a partial explanation, with rendering and stimulus statistics as other factors.
relationships.display_finding: The variability effect on CKA failed or remained unclear with large standard deviations; authors identified rendering and stimulus statistics as additional factors.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Figure D.4 identifies rotation exceptions with large SD, specifically layer4 for translation variability; Figures D.5–D.6 identify rotation exceptions for within-target layer4 similarity. These qualify the data-variability explanation.

relationships.condition: Same-target ResNet-18s with different seeds, layer4
relationships.reason: Seed-to-seed CKA in layer4 is higher with full than with reduced non-target variability (R11, R12). Seed convergence therefore depends on training-data diversity, with a rotation exception.
relationships.display_finding: Layer4 CKA was higher with full than reduced non-target variability, with an exception for rotation.

relation.reason: Reports its own between-target and within-target linear CKA results and manipulates non-target training-data variability.

tranche.reason: Tests convergence in a new setting: spatial versus category objectives on synthetic images, with controlled training-data variability. It does not reproduce the cross-modal scale experiment.

source_check.notes: Exact CKA values are not stated for these rows; their qualitative comparisons are supported by the prose and captions. The study does not establish a model-to-model scaling plateau or exclude learning a shared model of reality; the authors interpret their findings as compatible with learning world structure.
